author: /root/knot_concordance_algebraic_ribbon/hermitian_arithmetic_bound/zf_weakapprox_completions

findings: Finite CRT and archimedean lattice grid preserve the finite congruences after division by a common denominator.
Inverse-limit DVR construction proves completeness and density using specified residues, not countable choices.
Digit recursion gives free Zp rank e*f; finite-matrix diagonalization proves the usual determinant norm valuation.
Relative decomposition is obtained by base-field idempotents, not arbitrary valuation extension.

interfaces.weak_approximation: All finite lists of ideal-adic and real/complex embedding coordinates; scalar, nonzero scalar, and finite-dimensional vector versions.
interfaces.completion: Finite number-field completions, degrees e*f, tensor products over Qp and K_P, global/local determinant norms and traces, usual extending absolute value.
not_provided: Unramified quadratic extension and Frobenius/reduction classification
A theorem for arbitrary valuation extensions or complete valued fields

integration_caveat.actual_proof_reading: The corollary trace/norm proof already uses only its integral minimal polynomial and the finite companion-block characteristic polynomial f(X)^h; its embeddings dependency is unused. The embedding determinant can be specialized to the fixed complex field and finite roots, without arbitrary algebraic-closure existence.
integration_caveat.consequence: The donor arguments use finite arithmetic throughout, but no claim is made that the present canonical transitive dependency graph is Choice-free. Any canonical metadata hygiene or foundational specialization belongs to the owner/native integration scope.

claims_examined: Weak approximation and completion-valued version, Theorem 7.20
DVR residue and digit descriptions, Lemma 7.25 and Proposition 7.26
Discrete extension theorem 7.38, inspected to avoid importing its general interface
Finite local tensor and norm/trace decomposition, Propositions 8.1–8.2 and Corollary 8.4
